name: sgit
description: An independent brochure about sgit, git for encrypted vaults, for humans and AI agents, made from its own public pages.
headline: Version control for files the server must never read
lede: sgit lets people and AI agents clone, commit, branch and merge folders of files that are encrypted on their own machine before upload. The server holds only ciphertext, and a one-way read key lets anyone open a vault without an account.

quote.q: Git for encrypted vaults, for humans and AI agents

what.t: sgit is a command-line tool for folders of files that are encrypted with AES-256-GCM on your own machine before they are uploaded. You clone, commit, branch, diff and merge them much as you would with git.
The server stores only ciphertext under opaque IDs. It never sees filenames, file contents or commit messages.
A vault can be handed to someone with a single read key: no account, no hosting and nothing for the reader to install. The same vault opens in a browser through SG/Vault.
The code is free under Apache-2.0. What is sold is the running, maintained hosted service, at sgraph.ai; self-hosting is documented. sgit is marked beta.

story.t: sgit starts from one sentence on its own site: "you have files that need version control and collaboration, and the place they are stored must not be able to read them."
The package first appears on PyPI as version 0.8.17 on 20 March 2026. Releases came quickly through the spring, with more than thirty a month in April and May.
In August 2026 the project's own site began, at version 0.1.1 on 11 August, and the first published vaults followed on 16 August: real work shared openly with read keys.
By 13 October 2026 the site listed 54 published vaults and around 4,000 tests, and the SGit Newsroom had moved to its own address, newsroom.sgit.ai. Version 0.27.0 reached PyPI on 28 October 2026.
The site is candid about what it is not. It says it is in "daily production use by its authors, a small n", and tells anyone whose files are not sensitive to use git and a private repository instead.

for_whom.t: AI agents and the people working with them: agent state that must outlive the context window, shared between agents, with a human reviewing merges.
Professional services such as legal, M&A, audit and security assessment, handling client working documents.
Health and regulated sectors, where a host that provably cannot read the content changes what is allowed.
Not for everyone: if your files are not sensitive, the site says to use git and a private repository.

how.title: A folder becomes a vault
how.t: An ordinary folder gains a .sg_vault directory. A commit snapshots the whole folder; there is no staging area.

how.title: Encrypted on your machine
how.t: Every commit, tree and blob is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before upload, with keys derived by PBKDF2 at 600,000 iterations.

how.title: The server sees ciphertext
how.t: Objects are stored under opaque IDs. The server can see sizes and timing, never names or contents.

how.title: One string opens it
how.t: The vault key is address, credential and root of every key. A one-way read key decrypts but cannot write, so it can be published.

how.title: Merge, in terminal or browser
how.t: Each machine or agent gets a private branch; shared branches merge three ways. The browser app speaks the same format.

products.name: sgit
products.t: The command-line tool: pip install sgit-ai. Pure Python, Python 3.11 or newer, two runtime dependencies, Apache-2.0.

products.name: SG/Vault
products.t: A web app to browse and edit vaults and run their apps in the browser, an independent implementation of the same wire format.

products.name: SG/Send
products.t: The zero-knowledge storage and transfer API both clients speak to, hosted by sgraph.ai or self-hosted.

products.name: Published vaults
products.t: A catalogue of vaults with public read keys: 54 when last updated on 13 October 2026.

products.name: SGit Newsroom
products.t: Articles, a newsletter and a reading meter, at its own address since October 2026.
